Methods.Reason: Builds a 16-byte block from a big-endian 48-bit sequence, 48-bit serial number, 16-bit message tag and 16-bit payload length. High sequence bits are discarded.
Builds the sequence/serial/tag counter block with byte 14 set to 0xFF and byte 15 initially zero.

Clones the initial counter block, encrypts successive blocks with AES-128 ECB and increments only byte 15. Requests over 4096 bytes are rejected. Retains the original stream/padding and disposal behavior.

XORs the encrypted MAC with the start of the counter key stream and the encrypted payload with bytes after the reserved MAC block. Returns payload and outputs the plain MAC separately; this helper does not authenticate either result.
Builds the IP MAC block and delegates to the existing CBC-MAC helper with unencrypted-MAC output.
Builds the IP counter block and delegates to the existing encrypt helper with a 16-byte MAC reservation.
Separates the trailing 16 encrypted MAC bytes, decrypts payload and MAC, then concatenates both plain results. Authentication is performed by the frame caller.
Returns the retained or successfully decrypted inner frame.
Reads the 16-bit session identifier at the frame body start.
Reads the six-byte sequence/group timer value at body offset two.
Reads the six-byte serial number at body offset eight.
Reads the 16-bit message tag at body offset fourteen.
Returns successful authentication state, also initialized by keyed outgoing construction.
Reads the six-byte timer timestamp from the notification body start.
Reads the notification serial number at body offset six.
Reads the notification message tag at body offset twelve.
Returns the MAC comparison result or the keyed outgoing construction flag.

Decrypts payload/MAC and compares the received MAC with a recomputed MAC before parsing the inner frame and marking transport security. Caches success; a later different key is only logged and still returns true. Existing behavior is preserved.
Wraps a received frame and attempts decryption/authentication only when a key is supplied.
Serializes secure-wrapper session/sequence/serial/tag fields; with a key, computes and encrypts payload/MAC and marks the retained inner frame transport-secured.
Wraps the input and, if keyed, compares a calculated notification MAC with the 16 received bytes at absolute offset 20.
Serializes timer/serial/tag fields; with a key, writes the calculated notification MAC and marks the outgoing frame authentic.
Calculates the plain IP CCM MAC over the frame header with no payload, then encrypts that MAC using the notification timestamp, serial and message tag.
Captures the state and trigger used as a dictionary lookup key.
Extracts the declared state/trigger pair for construction of the transition lookup. Replaces the reviewed constructor-lambda alias with its actual selector behavior.
Requires state accessor/mutator, stores the logger, and indexes transitions by state/trigger. Duplicate transition keys retain ToDictionary failure behavior.
Looks up the current state/trigger, runs its action or state-returning action, and logs/mutates state only when changed. Missing transitions do nothing; action failures propagate.
Defines a fixed next-state transition with an optional action and explicit/default display name.
Defines a transition whose action computes the next state; initializes fallback next state to the current state.
Returns the event timestamp.
Returns the event serial number used to identify synchronization replies.
Returns the event message tag used to correlate synchronization replies.
Returns the acceptance decision set by the transition action.
Stores the acceptance decision returned by ReceivedSecureWrapper.
Captures timestamp, serial number and message tag for timer/secure-wrapper transition processing.
Converts the timing abstraction UTC time to unsigned Unix milliseconds.
Chooses an inclusive random delay between the bounds; when maximum is no greater than minimum returns maximum. Retains the int range conversion.
Promotes zero delay to one, stops the timer, divides the interval by the timing speed factor, records update/periodic purpose and restarts the one-shot timer.

Clears the update-scheduled flag and invokes the send callback. Replies reuse the captured request serial/tag; ordinary notifications generate a new random tag and use the local serial. Callback exceptions fault the task.
State-machine accessor reads the stored state directly.
State-machine mutator writes the stored state directly; logging belongs to the generic transition executor.
Selects the time-keeper or time-follower minimum periodic delay.
Selects the time-keeper or time-follower maximum periodic delay.
Selects the time-keeper or time-follower minimum update delay.
Selects the time-keeper or time-follower maximum update delay.
Reads the configured backbone timer synchronization trust mode.
Stores the ConnectMode setting consumed by the reviewed timer logic.
Reads the received-frame age tolerance.
Stores the LatencyTolerance setting consumed by the reviewed timer logic.
Reads the close-synchronization tolerance used in timestamp classification and derived delays.
Stores the SyncLatencyTolerance setting consumed by the reviewed timer logic.
Reads the lower initial-notification delay bound.
Stores the MinDelayInitialNotify setting consumed by the reviewed timer logic.
Reads the upper initial-notification delay bound.
Stores the MaxDelayInitialNotify setting consumed by the reviewed timer logic.
Reads the minimum periodic delay for a time keeper.
Stores the MinDelayTimeKeeperPeriodicNotify setting consumed by the reviewed timer logic.
Returns keeper periodic minimum plus three synchronization tolerances.
Returns keeper periodic maximum plus one synchronization tolerance.
Returns follower periodic minimum plus ten synchronization tolerances.
Reads the minimum update-notification delay for a time keeper.
Stores the MinDelayTimeKeeperUpdateNotify setting consumed by the reviewed timer logic.
Returns keeper update minimum plus one synchronization tolerance.
Returns keeper update maximum plus one synchronization tolerance.
Returns follower update minimum plus ten synchronization tolerances.
Reads whether this instance currently acts as the time keeper.
Stores the IsTimeKeeper setting consumed by the reviewed timer logic.
Reads whether the pending one-shot timer is for an update reply.
Stores the IsUpdateNotifyScheduled setting consumed by the reviewed timer logic.
Reads the stored notification scheduling state.
Logs and stores a state change only if it differs from the current state.
Applies artificial clock skew relative to its base, adds the timer offset and masks to the low 48 bits.
Resets the skew reference to current time and adjusts the offset to make the group timer equal the supplied value.
Changes the parts-per-million skew and resets its time base while retaining the current group timer value.
Adds an artificial millisecond offset; clamps a negative adjustment so the current group timer cannot become negative.
Encodes the time-keeper bit and scheduling state shifted by eight for diagnostics.
Only advances the group timer, logs its delta and increments the configured statistic when a collector exists.
Stores the notification callback, local serial and statistics context; initializes tolerances, one-shot timer and group timer zero.

With a nonzero initial maximum, schedules a randomized initial notification under the state lock. Otherwise sends immediately, then schedules a periodic notification. Records the initial time for synchronization waits.

Unless unsynchronized mode is configured, waits for a correlated/trusted response, forces one additional notification after the first timeout and waits again. Timeouts are swallowed; this method can complete without a valid response.
Only writes the existing A0 diagnostic; leaves timer/context unchanged.
Advances to the context timestamp. Completes synchronization only for a matching local serial/tag or trust-first-response mode.
Marks the context accepted; ReceivedSecureWrapper returns this result.
Chooses a periodic delay for the current keeper/follower role and arms a non-update notification.
Retains the triggering context and arms an update reply with a randomized role-dependent delay.
Starts a notification with the context timestamp and no reply identity. The returned task is deliberately not awaited here.
Starts a notification using the retained request identity, then clears it. The task is not awaited here.
Arms a non-update notification using the configured initial-delay range.
Sets the time-keeper role flag.
Clears the time-keeper role flag.
Updates/checks synchronization, becomes a follower, then schedules a periodic notification.
Becomes a follower and schedules the next periodic notification.
Updates/checks synchronization, accepts the wrapper, then schedules a periodic notification.
Updates/checks synchronization and accepts the wrapper, retaining the current notification schedule.
Accepts the wrapper and schedules a periodic notification.
Starts an ordinary notification, becomes time keeper and schedules a periodic notification without awaiting the send.
Starts the pending update reply, becomes time keeper and schedules a periodic notification without awaiting the send.
Under the state lock, classifies the received timestamp as ahead, within sync tolerance, within latency tolerance or too old, and fires the corresponding notification trigger.

Uses the same four timestamp categories under the state lock, fires the corresponding wrapper trigger and returns the context acceptance flag. This is age/state gating, not per-sender duplicate tracking.
Fires the sent-wrapper trigger under the state lock with the supplied timestamp and no reply identity.
Under the state lock, fires the elapsed trigger only for periodic/update scheduling states. Logs and swallows exceptions from processing.
Returns the current 16-bit tag and increments it with wraparound; does not add synchronization.

With a routing key, records secure-send statistics, allocates a message tag, captures group time, constructs an authenticated wrapper and notifies the timer of that send. Otherwise records a plain send and returns the original frame.
When a routing key exists, records notification statistics and forwards timestamp/serial/tag to the group timer. The caller has already checked authenticity.

Returns messages carried by routing indication/system-broadcast frames. Busy frames update send pacing under the connector lock; lost/unknown frames update diagnostics and return null. Unknown frames invoke the unhandled-frame delegate.

Applies system-broadcast policy, enforces configured secure/plain frame mode, validates wrapper/notification authentication and group-timer acceptance, then dispatches the inner/plain payload. Records each rejection and retains existing unhandled-frame callback behavior.

Processes a frame, suppresses one echo matching the pending confirmation by source/destination/length/APCI, then emits raw data and bus-message events outside Info mode. The comparison does not compare payload bytes.

With a routing key and connected communication, counts the outgoing notification, waits for send pacing and transmits a keyed timer notification. Missing security/communication returns successfully; asynchronous failures propagate.
